- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first 5–10 days, then plateau or slightly decline — but true values often spike higher later, especially after day 10.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., 47.00, 49.61), model fails to capture the subsequent sharp drop or mean reversion — overestimates continuation of the spike.
- Model tends to overreact to recent low prices (e.g., 35–38 range) by forecasting a prolonged recovery, but true values often show a more gradual or erratic rebound.
- Forecasts are generally too smooth — fail to capture volatility or sudden reversals in the true price series.
- Model exhibits a lag in responding to true price spikes — often forecasts a peak too early or too low.
- When true prices are below 40, model tends to forecast a recovery too quickly, often overshooting the actual low range.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price corrections after spikes — fails to recognize that prices often drop more than forecasted after a peak.
